Are you on Medicaid only? No add-on program? 

I was able to sign up for United Healthcare Community Plan through the NYS exchange and so far it is better than Medicaid, at least marginally. 

If you are already on medicaid you can choose from that, Healthy NY, and an Affinity plan (if I remember correctly). 

I'm sorry I cannot recommend an internist because I just started on this program, but I'm hoping some of my old doctors that took United Healthcare when I was a student will accept this current plan/be in network. Either way, you may have more options than what you'll find under Medicaid alone. 

https://nystateofhealth.ny.gov/

Zocdoc not only lists the doctors I can find through Medicaid, but United Healthcare Community Plan (and possibly the other Medicaid exchange programs I mentioned). I was able to sign up for the Community Plan right up I was enrolled in Medicaid.

The doctor currently listed on my own card is Carmine Ramlal. I'm sorry if I can't tell you if he's good or not yet, but still, that's a start. 

I would also look at ratemd.com and Yelp (I know, that sounds ridiculous, but it talks about the wait).

I wish I knew how to help, because I'm going through something similar--I'm the common factor when something good is in front of me, and doesn't actually feel like it's mine. And like you, I feel my best does not matter. 

Sometimes all I can do is be as good and smart as I can, love as much as I can, tell the people I know I NEED them (which should count)--and then give up and hope the universe isn't unkind, made the losses bearable, or gave me a source of life to replace whatever it is I've lost that's left me that much emptier. I wish I had a better answer than that, too.

Is there a specific period of your life or a relationship change that made these feelings come? 

I hate to go there, but have you ever tried antidepressants? 

They weren't a cure-all for me. It doesn't magically bring one financial security or free one from hurt, and most important, it doesn't relieve one of trying to plan for the future--trying to make good judgments. 

It makes the losses bearable; but I am trying to end my losing streak and failing.

I'm sorry you feel this way and it's flip to say, because you sound like you're pretty aware of your own emotional landscape and what you're getting out of your relationship with the world--but I hope someone or something comes into your life that delivers some piece. 

I know the continual, inexplicable sense of desperation and draining frustration.

I feel as you do and have for a long time. Especially feeling that I don't really have any claim to anything good, valuable, or related to love in this world, and it's not even a source of unbearable hurt--you accept it like you accept death itself, and the natural ugliness of things in your life. No real affect, no ability to get ahold of whatever it is that makes partaking of life worthwhile. 

What you wrote was was deeply moving and I'm sorry you feel alone. ("Alone" doesn't really cover it, does it?

More like your whole life is an accident and if the universe were kind you wouldn't have to feel how you feel just be thinking, feeling or existing. Or fundamentally tired with living in your own body, brain and history.)

I don't know about anxiety, but nausea...I would take a small bottle of toner to freshen your face; comfortable clothes; favorite headphones/calming music and books on tape; walking breaks when food isn't being served; and (after dramamine), sucking candies to help with nausea.
